takeaway: The medial and lateral circumflex arteries form the extracapsular arterial ring; it feeds the metaphysis and, through retinacular vessels, the femoral head.

question.text: An elderly woman presents with a fall and a tender right hip. Which of the following is true regarding the hip and neck of femur (NOF) fractures?
question.say: An elderly woman presents with a fall and a tender right hip. Which of the following is true regarding the hip and neck of femur fractures?

answer.text: Metaphyseal blood supply arises from the extracapsular arterial ring.

lines.text: An elderly woman falls and hurts her hip.
The medial and lateral circumflex arteries form a ring around the base of the femoral neck.
The medial circumflex is the most important.
From that extracapsular ring, retinacular vessels climb up the neck into the head.
The ring also sends branches to the metaphysis below.
The artery of the ligamentum teres is only a minor supply.
A neck fracture can tear these vessels and cause avascular necrosis.
So the metaphyseal supply comes from the extracapsular ring.
